verdict.rationale: Vercel's own docs show its functions accept portable, non-proprietary code: OCI container images built from a standard Dockerfile run on Vercel Functions, and WebSocket code uses the stock `ws` library with no extra configuration. Storage is also standard Postgres and Redis through providers like Neon and Upstash, since Vercel's proprietary KV and Postgres were retired. However, nothing documents a standards-based runtime API set (e.g. Web-standard Request/Response) promised to run unmodified across multiple edge platforms, and the Build Output API is a Vercel-specific spec. missing for 10: documented standard Web runtime API surface for functions or middleware, explicit cross-edge-platform portability claims, independent or hands-on corroboration of running unmodified elsewhere.

support.subject: As a developer, I can write code against standard runtime APIs so it runs unmodified across multiple edge platforms instead of being locked into proprietary storage/runtime APIs

citations.quote: Run any code and library on Vercel Functions with an OCI container image built from a Dockerfile or Containerfile at the project root.
WebSockets in Vercel Functions work exactly like any distributed WebSocket server, so you can use libraries like ws to upgrade connections with no additional configuration
Vercel KV is no longer available. If you had an existing Vercel KV store, we automatically moved it to Upstash Redis in December 2024.
